items.prompt: Return the length of the longest string that is a subsequence of both text1 and text2.
items.why: Two strings aligned against each other, skipping allowed → 2-D DP over the prefix pair (i, j).

items.prompt: Return the minimum number of insertions, deletions and replacements that turn word1 into word2.
items.why: 'Transform a into b' with per-operation costs → min-cost table over (i in word1, j in word2). Each operation is one neighbouring cell.

items.prompt: Return the length of the longest subsequence of a single string that reads the same forwards and backwards.
items.why: One string and a palindrome → interval DP on s[i..j], filled by length. Not a prefix pair of two different strings.

items.prompt: Given an integer array, find the maximum sum of a strictly increasing subsequence.
items.why: One sequence against itself: best subsequence ending at i, looking back at every j < i that can precede it (the PDF files it under this pattern). No capacity, so it isn't knapsack.

items.prompt: Find the length of the longest substring of s that contains no repeating characters.
items.why: One string, contiguous, and a condition you can maintain as the window moves → dynamic sliding window. There's no second string to align.

items.prompt: Given two strings, return the length of the longest substring (contiguous) that appears in both.
items.why: Two strings + contiguous → prefix-pair table where a cell is the common run ending at (i, j). A mismatch resets it to 0, and the answer is the max cell.

items.prompt: Can the array be split into two subsets with equal sums?
items.why: Pick-or-skip each item to hit a target sum (a capacity) → 0/1 Knapsack. The second DP index is a sum, not a position in another sequence.

items.prompt: Given two sorted arrays, return the elements that appear in both.
items.why: Sorted inputs, and you only ever advance → one pointer per array, O(n + m). No prefix pair is ever revisited, so no table is needed.
